record.paper_title: Frequently hypercyclic operators: recent advances and open problems
record.original_question: Must every chaotic operator be frequently hypercyclic? Here a chaotic operator is a hypercyclic operator with dense periodic points, whereas a frequently hypercyclic operator has some orbit that visits every nonempty open set with positive lower density.

evidence.quote:
Problem (Bayart-Grivaux). Is every chaotic operator frequently hypercyclic?
This problem has since been iterated in various articles, an d it has come to be considered
as one of the major questions in linear dynamics; see, for exa mple, [8, Chapter 6] and [43,
Chapter 9]. Menet [47] very recently obtained a counter-exa mple.
Theorem 15 (Menet). There exists a chaotic operator that is not frequently hyper cyclic.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a separable infinite-dimensional Banach space, and let $T:X\to X$ be a bounded linear operator. Say that $T$ is hypercyclic if there exists $x\in X$ whose orbit $\{T^n x: n\ge 0\}$ is dense in $X$. Say that $T$ is chaotic (in the sense of Devaney) if $T$ is hypercyclic and its set of periodic points $\{x\in X: T^n x=x \text{ for some } n\ge 1\}$ is dense in $X$. Say that $T$ is frequently hypercyclic if there exists $x\in X$ such that for every nonempty open set $U\subset X$, the set $\{n\ge 0: T^n x\in U\}$ has positive lower density, i.e. $\liminf_{N\to\infty} \frac{1}{N}\#\{0\le n<N: T^n x\in U\}>0$.

Question: Must every chaotic bounded linear operator on a separable infinite-dimensional Banach space be frequently hypercyclic?
artifact.status_search_result: The question (Bayart–Grivaux) was resolved in the negative by Q. Menet, who constructed a chaotic operator on $\ell^1$ that is not frequently hypercyclic (in fact, not even $\mathcal{U}$-frequently hypercyclic). The result appears in "Linear chaos and frequent hypercyclicity," Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 369 (2017).

status_evidence.title: Linear chaos and frequent hypercyclicity
status_evidence.snippet: Menet constructs a chaotic operator on ℓ¹ which is not U-frequently hypercyclic, answering a question of Bayart and Grivaux.
status_evidence.claim: A chaotic operator that is not frequently hypercyclic exists, so not every chaotic operator is frequently hypercyclic.

status_evidence.title: Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 369 (2017)
status_evidence.snippet: Published version of Menet's counterexample to the Bayart–Grivaux question.
status_evidence.claim: The negative answer is published in the Transactions of the AMS.
